A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT-RVS work and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Existing content can be matched despite layout changes and an added appendix.

before.justification: v3 reports original CoT-RVS benchmark results, keyframe-selection ablations, efficiency measurements and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a component-substitution experiment in Appendix H, Table A5.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline, default components, offline and online procedures, Equations (1)–(12), and prompts remain unchanged. LISA and Cutie are evaluated as substitutions within the existing modular framework; no revised algorithm is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MeViS, Refer-DAVIS-2017, ReasonVOS, ReVOS, T-ReasonVOS and the same video segmentation scenarios. The new modularity experiment uses the already evaluated Refer-DAVIS-2017 task.

E2.justification: Table A5 adds comparison variants combining LISA-13B-Llama2 or Seg-Zero-7B with Cutie or SAM2, alongside the default configuration. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark, efficiency and keyframe-selector comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix H introduces a controlled comparison of two image segmenters and two video processors on Refer-DAVIS-2017, fixing the keyframe selector to Gemma3-12B. Existing evaluation settings, sampling rules and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds an ablation testing whether the image segmentation and video processing modules can be substituted independently or together. Existing CoT, sampling, efficiency, robustness and failure-case analyses are retained, including material shifted to later appendix letters.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for the experiments. Table A5 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table A5 newly reports J&F scores of 68.8 for LISA-13B-Llama2/Cutie, 71.1 for LISA-13B-Llama2/SAM2, and 72.1 for Seg-Zero-7B/Cutie, using Gemma3-12B on Refer-DAVIS-2017. Its default score of 74.6 repeats Table 2. Existing Tables 1–6 and A1–A4 and qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, mask constraints, Equations (1)–(12), and Appendix F's latency derivation remain unchanged. No new assumptions, propositions or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free CoT reasoning, modularity, temporal keyframe selection and online segmentation. The new experiment supports an existing modularity claim.

C2.justification: Appendix G specifies that its unchanged valid-output analysis measures offline CoT prompt adherence, replacing the broader description of reliability. New Appendix H interprets component substitutions as preserving performance sufficiently to demonstrate modularity. Existing limitations and failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: v4 removes the abstract's repository pointer and the Reproducibility Statement, including its release-upon-acceptance commitment. Appendix D still promises the dataset and selection code, and existing prompts, hardware and implementation settings remain. Table A5 additionally identifies the precise segmentation model variants.

R1.justification: v4 adds Cheng et al. (2024), Putting the Object Back into Video Object Segmentation, for Cutie. LISA was already cited and evaluated in v3. The related-work discussion and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include publication-header and affiliation updates, added implementation cross-references, a localized Appendix G clarification, insertion of Modularity Analysis and removal of the Reproducibility Statement. Subsequent appendices are relabeled; most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table A5, rearranges the author block, moves Figure 1 from page 1 to page 2 and Figure A6 from page 22 to page 23, and reflows surrounding material. Existing figures and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix H supplies direct evidence for substituting both downstream modules, strengthening the existing modularity claim beyond v3's keyframe-selector comparisons. Appendix G also describes its measurement more precisely. These are limited gains: the new study covers one benchmark, alternatives score below the default, and removal of the repository pointer weakens access guidance. With detailed implementation information retained, the net improvement is modest.
